independent_verification.test_suite: godot --headless -s res://tests/run_tests.gd -> SUITE RESULT: PASS (0 failure(s)), exit 0 (Godot 4.7.1.stable)
independent_verification.separation_runtime: min pairwise arc 0.0848 rad = 0.678 units (n25/n30); 13 pairs < 1.9-unit hitbox diameter; claimed 0.25 rad floor never applied
independent_verification.lsp: no genuine diagnostics on all 17 GDScript files; only environmental 'hides a global script class' noise from shared language server

findings.title: Node-separation formula never applies the documented 0.25 rad minimum — shipped world has 13 node pairs with overlapping pick hitboxes (min 0.68 units apart vs 1.9-unit hitbox diameter)
findings.detail: sep(attempt=0) = 0.25*0.25 = 0.0625 = the floor, so separation is a constant 0.0625 rad (~0.5 units at R=8) and the decay is dead code. Runtime-verified at seed 20260904: min pairwise separation 0.0848 rad = 0.678 units (n25/n30) vs the 1.9-unit hitbox diameter — 13 pairs overlap. Falsifies the PR body's 'node separation 0.25 rad keeps the 0.95-radius hitboxes non-overlapping' and the spec's 'separation floor keeps hitboxes disjoint'. Presses on visually empty surface inside an inflated overlapping sphere begin DRAW instead of ORBIT, undermining the epic's 'input disambiguation never misfires' contract in practice.
findings.recommended_fix: Drop the MAXF_SEPARATION_FLOOR factor from the sep formula (sep := MIN_NODE_SEPARATION_RAD * (1.0 - float(attempt)/80.0), floored at 0.25*MIN). Re-run the suite and regenerate captures; verify min pairwise arc >= ~0.24 rad.

findings.title: Connect-verb gesture lifecycle (draw_begin/draw_move/draw_end/draw_cancel) has zero test coverage — the release-driven commit and cancel-elsewhere paths are unverified
findings.detail: grep-verified: no test references draw_begin/draw_move/draw_end/draw_cancel; only the programmatic shortcut connect_programmatic is exercised. E1.3's release-to-connect / cancel-elsewhere behavior — the slice's primary verb — is untested, and two confirmed latent bugs (stale _last_preview_end; stale snap-target commit) live inside exactly this untested region.
findings.recommended_fix: Add headless tests driving the real gesture path on the instantiated main scene: draw_begin on a node, draw_move projections, release-on-node commits, release-elsewhere cancels, focus-loss cancels.

findings.title: Advisory test gate: FAIL
findings.evidence:
var scripts := [
	"res://tests/test_geodesic.gd",
	"res://tests/test_camera.gd",
	"res://tests/test_input.gd",
	"res://tests/test_no_sim.gd",
findings.detail: Gate roll-up of the coverage lens: P0 critical path (connect-verb gesture lifecycle, happy + core cancel path) below 100% -> FAIL per the skill's gate thresholds. The 36 passing checks pin the math/camera/classify/no-sim contracts but not the gesture state machine.
findings.recommended_fix: Close the gesture-lifecycle gap (see connect_controller.gd blocker); gate rises to PASS.

findings.title: Placement last-resort loop never retries: fallback position is computed once and returned even when it violates separation
findings.detail: fallback is computed once outside the loop; the 10 iterations re-check the identical point, and the unconditional final 'return fallback' ignores the result anyway. The documented '10 more tries' honoring 50% separation is ornamental.
findings.recommended_fix: Move the fallback computation inside the loop (new rng draws per attempt) or delete the loop; only return positions that pass the separation check, else push_error.

findings.title: Pinch zoom is specified (epic E1.2 'scroll/pinch'; spec matrix 'Scroll/pinch') but no gesture branch exists — trackpad pinch silently does nothing
findings.evidence:
if event is InputEventMouseButton and event.pressed \
		and (event.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_UP or event.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_DOWN):
findings.detail: Only mouse-wheel buttons are mapped to zoom_requested. InputEventMagnifyGesture (macOS trackpad pinch) and pan gestures are unhandled, so the E1.2 'scroll/pinch zoom through the ladder' contract is half-delivered.
findings.recommended_fix: Handle InputEventMagnifyGesture (factor -> ladder step) or document the deferral of pinch to E7 explicitly in the PR/spec.

findings.title: Spec artifact declares status 'done' while its A3 Godot-MCP verification task is still unchecked
findings.evidence:
status: 'done'
...
- [ ] Godot MCP loop: `lsp-diagnostics` clean on all GDScript; `editor-run` + `debug-output` boot check, iterate on errors -- A3
findings.detail: Frontmatter says done; the task covering briefing item A3 ('verified, not claimed') is unchecked. Reviewer independently ran import + headless suite (clean, exit 0) and LSP diagnostics (no genuine errors/warnings — only environmental 'hides a global script class' noise from a shared language server), so the substance holds, but the shipped tracker contradicts itself.
findings.recommended_fix: Check the A3 box (or mark it superseded) so the artifact's status matches its task list.

findings.title: Headless suite hangs forever instead of failing when staged-world regressions occur: unguarded sites[0..3] indexing after a soft check()
findings.evidence:
var a: NodeSite = sites[0]
	var b: NodeSite = sites[1]
findings.detail: check(sites.size() == 33) only records a failure and execution continues; an empty/short sites array triggers an out-of-bounds runtime error that aborts run_all, then 'failures += null' aborts _run_once — quit() never runs and CI hangs instead of reporting FAIL.
findings.recommended_fix: Early-return from run_all when sites.size() < 4 (after recording the failure), or guard each index use.

findings.title: InputRouter integration path untested — only the pure classify() rule is pinned; _pick physics query, mode transitions, and focus-loss cancel have no tests
findings.evidence:
func _pick(screen_pos: Vector2) -> Dictionary:
	var from := camera.project_ray_origin(screen_pos)
findings.detail: test_input.gd pins classify() only. The collision mask (0b11, areas+bodies), _begin/_end mode transitions, and the NOTIFICATION_WM_WINDOW_FOCUS_OUT cancel path are unverified.
findings.recommended_fix: Add an integration test with a real collider + Area3D: press-on-node begins DRAW, press-on-body begins ORBIT, focus-out mid-gesture emits gesture_cancelled.

findings.title: E1.5 node orientation and collision setup untested — suite asserts only node count and wedge spread
findings.evidence:
func _orient_to_surface() -> void:
	var n := surface_pos.normalized()
findings.detail: No test verifies buildings are oriented to the surface normal (basis.y ~= normal) or that the Area3D sits on collision layer 2 — the property the input grammar depends on.
findings.recommended_fix: Assert site.global_transform.basis.y ~= surface normal for sampled sites and collision_layer == 2.

findings.title: draw_end never resets _last_preview_end (draw_cancel does) — a re-draw whose first projected end lands within 1e-4 of the previous gesture's end skips the rebuild and the preview stays invisible for that span
findings.evidence:
_source = null
_snap_target = null
_preview.visible = false
findings.detail: Reset-state inconsistency between the cancel and end paths; self-heals on the next motion event, so impact is a rare transient preview hiccup.
findings.recommended_fix: Reset _last_preview_end = Vector3.INF in draw_end (and draw_begin) for symmetry with draw_cancel.

findings.title: draw_end commits the last motion event's snap target — the release point itself is never re-snapped
findings.detail: A flick-release with no intervening motion event commits to a node the pointer may already have left. Usually harmless (last-hovered = intent), but the release projection is computed and then used only for the sky check.
findings.recommended_fix: Re-run snap_candidate on the release projection when it hits the surface, and commit to that (falling back to cancel).

findings.title: Signal orbit_started is emitted but never connected anywhere
findings.evidence: signal orbit_started
findings.detail: grep-verified: declaration (input_router.gd:10) and emit (:64) only; main.gd connects every other router signal. Dead signal.
findings.recommended_fix: Connect it or delete it.

findings.title: capture_runner._arc_mid scales an already-radius-length vector by PLANET_RADIUS again
findings.evidence:
var mid := Geodesic.geodesic_points(a.global_position, b.global_position, 2)[1]
	return mid * WorldSeed.PLANET_RADIUS
findings.detail: geodesic_points returns |a|-length points (~8.08); the extra *8 yields ~65 units. Every current caller normalizes, masking the error — latent only.
findings.recommended_fix: Return mid directly (drop the * PLANET_RADIUS).

findings.title: Capture 02 comment promises nearest-neighbor framing; code uses the 0.65-rad pair
findings.detail: Comment and code disagree (stale comment).
findings.recommended_fix: Update the comment to describe _readable_pair.

findings.title: Capture 01 frames with the normalized-sum trick on the MOST antipodal pair — the same file's _arc_mid docstring flags that trick as degenerate for opposite pairs
findings.evidence:
var spread := _most_spread_pair(sites)
var frame_p: Vector3 = ((spread[0] as Node3D).global_position + (spread[1] as Node3D).global_position) * 0.5
findings.detail: For a near-antipodal pair the sum approaches zero and the frame direction is ill-defined (seed-dependent). The shipped seed's capture is fine; a different seed could silently produce a broken globe shot.
findings.recommended_fix: Use _arc_mid(spread[0], spread[1]) for the frame point too.

findings.title: 'No Sim autoload registered' check is vacuous — get_setting('autoload', {}) always returns the default
findings.evidence: var project_sim: Variant = ProjectSettings.get_setting("autoload", {})
findings.detail: Runtime-verified: has_setting('autoload') == false (autoloads register as 'autoload/<Name>'), so this check can never fail. The other two no-sim checks (group scan, method-name scan) are substantive, so the contract still holds.
findings.recommended_fix: Check ProjectSettings for any key beginning 'autoload/' instead.

findings.title: Merged-bundle radius and elevation grow unbounded; only the strand count is capped
findings.evidence: return [1.0 + 0.45 * float(count - 1), mini(3 * count, 9)]
findings.detail: Every extra parallel pipe adds 0.45 to the radius scale and raises the elevation proportionally; 20 pipes = 9.5x cable. No gameplay cap exists in E1.
findings.recommended_fix: Cap the radius scale (and document the cap), e.g. minf(1.0 + 0.45*(count-1), 3.0).

findings.title: 'Merged bundle keeps the same geodesic path' test checks only the endpoints while the merged rebuild also scales elevation
findings.evidence: check(vapprox(arc._a, a.global_position, 1e-5) and vapprox(arc._b, b.global_position, 1e-5), "merged bundle keeps the same geodesic path")
findings.detail: Endpoints never change by construction, so the assertion is weak; the mid-arc ground track (normalized direction) is what 'same path' means.
findings.recommended_fix: Assert mid-arc sample directions match between single and merged builds (normalize away the elevation).

findings.title: Cloud puff offset salt omits the cloud index — all four clouds share one puff layout
findings.evidence: mi.position = Vector3(puff * 0.7 - 0.7, WorldSeed.unit_f(_seed, 45000 + puff) * 0.3, 0)
findings.detail: Every neighboring draw salts with the cloud index i (41000+i ... 44000+i*10+puff); 45000+puff does not, so all clouds have identical puff offsets. Cosmetic.
findings.recommended_fix: Salt with 45000 + i * 10 + puff.

findings.title: geodesic_axis/_deterministic_perp comment claims the 'least aligned' axis; the code only avoids the dominant one
findings.evidence:
## Deterministic for parallel and antipodal inputs: picks the world axis
## least aligned with `a` (X, then Y, then Z) crossed with a.
findings.detail: Z-dominant input falls through to AXIS_X even when Y is less aligned; the result is still perpendicular and deterministic, so behavior is correct — the docstring overstates.
findings.recommended_fix: Reword the comment ('avoids the axis most aligned with a').

findings.title: World seed 20260904 is duplicated as bare literals throughout test_no_sim
findings.evidence: biomes[WorldSeed.biome_at(WorldSeed.wedge_layout(20260904), 20260904, s.surface_pos)] = true
findings.detail: main.gd owns 'const SEED := 20260904'; tests hardcode the literal. Changing the game seed silently makes the biome/determinism checks test a world the game no longer builds.
findings.recommended_fix: Reference a shared constant (e.g. load main.gd's SEED) in the tests.

findings.title: Shipped slice stages 33 nodes against the GDD's 'Planet — MVP node count 4–6' (gdd.md:327); the 'bigger planet, many buildings' justification is user direction per the PR body but is not in the epic/briefing inputs
findings.evidence: # 2 routers + 9 houses per wedge — a world with MANY connectables.
findings.detail: Fact-verified: gdd.md:327 sets MVP node count 4–6; the epic (spec of record) pins no count and the PR body cites explicit user direction. Recorded so the deviation is conscious, not silent.
findings.recommended_fix: Note the user direction in the spec artifact (it currently appears only in the PR body) so future reviewers can trace it.

findings.title: Geodesic is documented as 'pure static math' but snap_candidate takes/returns scene-tree Node3D
findings.evidence: static func snap_candidate(point: Vector3, candidates: Array, snap_arc: float) -> Node3D:
findings.detail: Couples the math spine to scene-tree types; a pure variant (positions in, index out) would keep the module honest and equally testable.
findings.recommended_fix: Overload with a positions-only variant, or move snap_candidate to the controller.

findings.title: Scripts self-resolve sibling scene paths ('../OrbitRig', '../Nodes') instead of composition-root injection
findings.evidence: @onready var rig: OrbitCamera = get_node("../OrbitRig")
findings.detail: Works for the fixed scene layout; brittle to re-parenting and untestable in isolation. Idiomatic for Godot, noted for later slices.
findings.recommended_fix: Have main.gd inject dependencies (controller.rig = rig) or use unique-name node lookups.

findings.title: Dev-only capture harness is instantiated inside the shipped main scene
findings.evidence: [node name="CaptureRunner" type="Node" parent="."]
findings.detail: Inert without -- --capture, so harmless in play; but the shipped scene carries dev tooling. Acceptable for slice 1; revisit when the scene ships to players.
findings.recommended_fix: Move capture composition to a separate scene that extends main, or add the node only in debug builds.

findings.title: Geodesic.ray_sphere ships in production but its only callers are tests
findings.evidence: static func ray_sphere(origin: Vector3, dir: Vector3, center: Vector3, radius: float) -> Vector3:
findings.detail: grep-verified: production ray-casts use physics (space.intersect_ray); ray_sphere is exercised solely by test_geodesic. Either future API or dead weight.
findings.recommended_fix: Keep with a 'reserved for E2+' note, or drop it and let the tests use physics.

findings.title: Orthonormal-basis idiom and elevated_path computation are duplicated across node_site/pipe_arc (and computed twice per pipe rebuild)
findings.evidence:
var helper := Vector3.UP if absf(n.dot(Vector3.UP)) < 0.99 else Vector3.RIGHT
	var t1 := n.cross(helper).normalized()
findings.detail: Same basis-from-normal idiom in two modules; pipe_arc._rebuild_mesh and _rebuild_trestles each recompute the identical elevated_path.
findings.recommended_fix: Factor the basis idiom into Geodesic; compute the path once in build() and pass it down.

findings.title: Pipe-bundle registry keys bundles by node display names
findings.detail: Works because generated names are unique; instance-id keys would be robust to renames and freed nodes (a freed node's name could be reused by a future node).
findings.recommended_fix: Key by instance_id (sorted pair) instead of name.

findings.title: test_input.gd leaks a Camera3D — engine reports leaked ObjectDB instances and a Camera RID at suite exit
findings.evidence: check(InputRouter.classify(Camera3D.new()) == InputRouter.Mode.ORBIT, "any non-node collider = ORBIT")
findings.detail: Byte-verified against reviewer suite output: 'WARNING: 2 ObjectDB instances were leaked at exit' / 'ERROR: 1 RID allocations of type CameraE were leaked'. The ad-hoc Camera3D.new() is never freed. Cosmetic, but it trains the suite to tolerate leak noise.
findings.recommended_fix: Instantiate into a var and free() it after the check.

findings.title: Spec task list references nonexistent tools/capture.gd; actual file is scripts/capture_runner.gd
findings.evidence: - [x] `tools/capture.gd` + `captures/` -- the four committed captures -- A4
findings.detail: The code map in the same file gets it right; the task line is stale.
findings.recommended_fix: Fix the path in the task list.

findings.title: capture_runner ignores save/dir error codes — a failed capture still prints success and exits 0
findings.evidence:
img.save_png(ProjectSettings.globalize_path(path))
	print("capture: %s (%d KB)" % [file_name, int(img.get_data().size() / 1024.0)])
findings.detail: save_png's Error return is unchecked (as is make_dir_recursive_absolute's), so a disk/permission failure produces a green run and missing PNGs.
findings.recommended_fix: Check the return codes; push_error and quit(1) on failure.

rejected_findings.title: draw_move's 1e-4 rebuild guard is a no-op at real zooms
rejected_findings.reject_reason: Claim contradicts actual behavior: while a snap target is held, 'end' is the constant node position, so the guard skips rebuilds on every motion event inside the snap radius — the guard is load-bearing, not a no-op.
